fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
‍

Module 5 focuses on the elements informing the development of a robust maintenance program, which aims at physical assets performing safely, capably, reliably, and repeatedly to their desired performance in their given operating context. Introductory topics include failure definitions, the fundamentals of a maintenance program, and asset criticality analysis, followed by the main types of maintenance and their associated tasks. The second part of the microcredential deals with processes and methodologies used to develop a maintenance program. fieldData.course-description: Fundamentals of Real Estate is the first course required in becoming a licensed real estate professional in Alberta.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
Fundamentals of Real Estate is the first course required to become a licensed real estate professional in Alberta. The course provides the foundational knowledge and competencies a successful real estate practitioner must know and prepares students for the Real Estate Licensing exam. An overview of real estate along with the related Real Estate Act, Rules, Regulations, and applicable contract and real property laws are explored. Students delve into the concepts of ethics, professionalism, and risk reduction, as well as the multi-facets of consumer relationships. Further topics of mortgage financing and fraud awareness, property valuation, real estate brokerages, and condominiums are discussed providing a solid foundational knowledge for the real estate practitioner.

‍

Real Estate Licensing Eligibility:

Students wanting to become licensed in real estate in Alberta, must first meet the Real Estate Council of Alberta (RECA) eligibility requirements. Visit the RECA's Getting Licensed information page for more details.

  1. Complete the eligibility process with RECA.
  2. Once RECA approves your eligibility, enroll in he courses you wish to take at Bow Valley College. Please note that you will need to submit your REA eligibility approval confirmation to the college.
  3. Check your email for confirmation of your course registration.

‍

Course Features:
  • Pre-requisites: None
  • Course Delivery: Self-paced online study with access to an industry expert instructor.  
  • Course Schedule: Six months to complete the course. A recommended 15-week course is provided in the course outline.
  • Course length: 80-110 hours based on learners' existing knowledge, experience in the industry, and active engagement with learner supports.
  • Completion Requirements: A minimum of 70% is required to pass the course.
  • Language of instruction: English
  • Accreditation: Officially recognized by RECA as an approved course
  • Validity: 3 months to write RECA’s pre-licensing exam upon completing this course

‍

RECA Licensing Exam:

Students must meet the RECA Eligibility requirements and successfully pass this course. Students will need to successfully complete RECA examination to become licensed.

  • Exam: Administered by RECA. See RECA’s Exam Guide to learn more.
  • Exam Length: 3 hours
  • Exam attempts: 2
  • Passing Grade: 70%
For students not interested in becoming a real estate licensee:

If you want to take the real estate courses for general interest and do not intend to become a licensee, you do not need to register with RECA. However, we will require you to sign a declaration letter.

  • Chain of Survival
  • 1-rescuer/2-rescuer CPR
  • High-quality chest compressions with feedback device
  • Multi-rescuer team CPR
  • Adult, child, and infant CPR and relief of choking
  • Use of an AED
  • Effective ventilations using barrier device and bag-mask device
  • EXPANDED: Opioid-associated life-threatening emergencies
  • NEW: Role of the CPR coach; Maternal cardiac arrest; Anaphylaxis; Drowning; Heart attack and stroke; and other life-threatening emergencies
